data.goal: Close the Rectify loop: one click on any sent History batch re-captures the live device, diffs it per annotation against the batch's stored frozen frame (pixel-region change-evidence plus an F-5 layout-finding oracle), renders a per-annotation Fixed / Still off verdict, and re-stages exactly the still-off annotations back through F-7's send path — persisting Verified / Follow-up sent through F-8's so-far-unused HistoryRepository.updateStatus hook.
data.problemStatement: F-8 shipped a Verify button gated to BatchStatusModel.Fixed, but nothing in v1 ever writes Fixed, so the button is dead on arrival (MirrorHistoryTab.kt:178-186) and the PRD's strongest differentiator — per-annotation, per-region pixel + hierarchy verification — is unbuilt. Users cannot confirm an agent's fix landed without eyeballing two screenshots, and have no tight way to push back just the annotations that are still wrong.
data.highLevelDescription: Four real gaps, everything else is reuse. (1) Read one batch WITH its annotations: HistoryEntryWithAnnotations already carries the data, the read mapper drops it — add @Transaction @Query findById(String) to HistoryEntryDao (ReadableDataSource.getById is Int-keyed and useless), HistoryDataSource.getBatch, HistoryRepository.get(batchId): SentBatchModel? (the existing write-path model reused as the read model), GetSentBatchUseCase / UpdateBatchStatusUseCase. (2) Read bytes off disk: BatchFileStore is write-only, so a new `fun interface BatchFileReader { suspend fun read(path: String): ByteArray? }` with a java.io desktop impl and null-returning Android/iOS stand-ins — the one genuinely new seam. (3) Pixel diff: pure IntArray arithmetic in commonMain (RegionDiff.changedRatio) fed by a ~10-line ImageBitmap.readPixels edge function, with NO PixelDiffer seam of any kind — a seam would push the arithmetic into desktopMain where desktopTest has no Skiko and destroy unit-testability. (4) densityDpi is not persisted: take it from the fresh AFTER dump and apply it to both sides — no column, no migration, no schema change. The UI is a new MirrorStage.Verify case rendered inside the ONE existing MirrorHost/MirrorContent composition, with the BEFORE/AFTER bitmaps delivered on a new plain StateFlow<VerifyFrames?> as a 5th content-lambda argument (a ~2-line RectifyWindow.kt edit). Verdict: Fixed iff nodeMatched && afterFinding == null && (regionPx < MIN_REGION_PIXELS || changedRatio > REGION_CHANGE_RATIO) — change-evidence, because the literal AC-24 wording would report an agent that did nothing as having fixed the bug.
data.background: F-5 shipped a measure-mode toolkit (snapTarget, projectMeasureNodes, measure, findingOf, deltaLabel, plainValueLabel, displayDelta, SEPARATOR) that is exactly the layout oracle this feature needs — the hierarchy half of the diff is measure() on both sides plus one comparison, and the design's own result strings ('top Δ6dp → 0dp', 'height 24dp → 32dp · want 48dp') decompose verbatim into those functions. F-7 shipped resolveAndSend()/assembleEnvelope/CropEncoder, which the follow-up re-enters unchanged except for one pendingFollowUpBatchId hook. F-8 shipped the history tables, the on-disk ~/.rectify/history/<batchId>/{frame.png,hierarchy.xml,crop-<i>.png} layout, all five BatchStatusModel values and the zero-caller updateStatus hook, and presentation-core-ui already ships VerificationRow/VerificationOutcome whose own @Preview uses the design's exact strings. The three corrections of record carried from Preparation (no PixelDiffer seam; AC-24 change-evidence semantics; AS-1 requires an active mirror session) were forced by the codebase recon after clarify closed and are honoured here verbatim.

assumptions: AS-1 [AMENDED — correction #3, false as originally written]: there is no on-demand capture pipeline. StartMirroringUseCase is stream-only and no one-shot capture use case exists. Verify therefore requires an active mirror session on the device: it reads MirrorViewModel.currentHeld.value atomically (the same freezing pattern stageAnnotation already uses) and fails with VerifyError.NoLiveSession otherwise.

AS-2: the device used for Verify is the same device that was mirrored when the batch was sent; v1 does not re-target a disconnected/replaced device (deviceLabel is a display label, not a serial, and is not used to enforce this).
AS-3: F-5's node matching runs headlessly against a stored hierarchy snapshot; findingOf is reused directly as the layout oracle — no new matching algorithm.

AS-4: F-8's persisted frame.png and hierarchy.xml are sufficient diff inputs; densityDpi is the one known gap and is addressed via the AFTER-dump fallback, not a schema change. crop files are not read at all.

AS-5: PRD Stage-4's resolution ('Verify is available on any sent batch regardless of status; History status chips remain informational only') is authoritative and supersedes F-8's AC-36 outright; this plan does not re-open it.

ImageBitmap.readPixels(buffer, startX, startY, width, height, bufferOffset, stride) is a commonMain member (proven by the existing FakeFrameBitmap overriding that exact signature), so a region read is just the annotation rect as arguments.

FR-46's single frame-size check collapses both sides onto ONE IntSize and ONE density, which is what makes projectMeasureNodes safe to call with a shared frame size and makes one density for both sides coherent.

constraints.text: No second MirrorHost call site. Verify is a new stage rendered inside the existing MirrorHost/MirrorContent composition (presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md Deviation 1: there is no Destination for this surface and there will not be one).

[AMENDED — correction #1] Pixel diffing is pure IntArray arithmetic in commonMain (RegionDiff.changedRatio) with a ~10-line ImageBitmap.readPixels edge function. No PixelDiffer seam of any kind — not expect/actual, not a fun interface. BatchFileReader is the one genuinely new seam and only reads bytes off disk.

Skiko trap: presentation-feature-mirror's desktopTest has no Skiko native library, so ImageBitmap(w, h) throws LibraryLoadException there. Exactly ONE file (core/verify/RegionPixels.kt) may mention ImageBitmap; everything else takes IntArrays. No test ever constructs a bitmap.
The diff reads the full-resolution stored frame.png only — never crop-N.png, never the ≤128px thumbnail BLOB (AC-45).

Hierarchy/layout diffing reuses F-5's snapTarget / projectMeasureNodes / measure / findingOf / deltaLabel / plainValueLabel / displayDelta / SEPARATOR in place (they are internal to presentation-feature-mirror). Never copy them out, never reimplement unit conversion.

[CORRECTED — the recon was wrong here] Adding the Verify stage DOES require a ~2-line RectifyWindow.kt edit: the MirrorHost content lambda widens by one parameter (a 5th StateFlow<VerifyFrames?>), the same precedent as its earlier 3→4 widening for frozenHierarchy.

Pixels never enter reduced state (presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md Deviation 2). VerifyFrames rides a plain StateFlow beside frame/frozenFrame; MirrorUiState.history remains the only audited exception and is not extended.

No database schema change or migration. database.md requires a @Database version bump AND a hand-written Migration for any new column, and F-8's stay-at-version-1 was a one-off explicitly flagged as NOT reusable. densityDpi comes from the fresh AFTER dump.

domain-layer / error-handling: one-shot operations return Result<T>, reactive ones return a bare Flow<T> (never Flow<Result<T>>); every *UseCaseImpl body runs inside resultLauncher(errorMapper = Failure.Technical::Database), never raw runCatching. Mappers never throw; null-on-failure is universal — a failed image never fails the operation.

orbit-mvi (mirror's local precedent): handleIntent dispatches to private handlers, each `= intent { reduce {}; postSideEffect() }`; the container(...) trailing lambda is init-time only. package-layout + explicitApi(): core/ is internal-only, source/ is public, explicit visibility AND return type everywhere.
koin-di: one module per Gradle module; initKoin()'s load order is significant — append new bindings within their existing layer group, never reorder.

localisation: every piece of copy is a Res.string.* key resolved at the call site (VerificationRow.outcomeLabel takes a raw String, so the localised word is resolved by the caller). Key convention mirror_verify_*; no AAPT-style \' escapes in strings.xml.

testing: no comma or colon in backtick test names (they fail compileTestKotlinIosArm64); desktop is the target that runs; :compose-application has no test wiring, so nothing testable may live there; no Compose UI-test harness exists, so the stage is covered by light/dark @Preview pairs per compose-preview-convention.md.

design-tokens: no literal Color(0x…), no raw .dp, no hardcoded TextStyle at a call site. Verdict colours are Theme.color.sentFixed / warnStillOff, which are already identical in light and dark — NFR-9 is satisfied by using them and adding no new token.
Desktop (macOS) only in v1, matching F-7/F-8 and NFR-10.

dumpHierarchy costs ~2.7 s on a Pixel 8 and measure() is ~100 ms per 300-node dump (×2 per annotation), so the run must be cancellable and visibly staged — a naive implementation reads as a frozen window.

dependencies.note: The one-click follow-up reuses resolveAndSend() / MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend / assembleEnvelope / CropEncoder / mintSessionId unchanged except for one pendingFollowUpBatchId hook on the success path. Crops come from the AFTER frame for free because assembleEnvelope crops the current frozen held bitmap.

Consumes HistoryRepository.updateStatus (zero callers today), the stored frame.png/hierarchy.xml, BatchStatusModel.Verified/FollowUpSent (already persisted and rendered, no schema change) and the inert MirrorIntent.VerifyBatch stub + verifyBatch handler seam. Inherits two review findings: the 0-vs-1-based crop index (resolved by never reading crops, FR-47) and observeAll's missing LIMIT (explicitly NOT to be copied into findById).

The hierarchy half IS F-5: snapTarget matches the node on both frames, projectMeasureNodes projects both snapshots against the one shared frame size, measure()/findingOf is the layout oracle, and deltaLabel/plainValueLabel/displayDelta/SEPARATOR produce the design's result strings verbatim. Only one before→after formatter is missing.

risks.text: Threshold tuning is unvalidated (MET-3). CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR / REGION_CHANGE_RATIO / MIN_REGION_PIXELS are a first guess reasoned from antialiasing, caret and scroll cases, not measured.
risks.mitigation: Three named consts in one file, each KDoc'd with its ceiling and tuning method; 'Mark all as verified' is always available as the human override; recorded unverified-in-v1 per NFR-17; the golden-corpus upgrade path (a hand-labelled before/after corpus under commonTest/resources replayed by one parameterised test) is written down, not built.

risks.text: A display-override device (the documented Pixel 8 984×2132-vs-1080×2400 case) makes projectMeasureNodes discard the whole hierarchy, which would otherwise emit N confident, wrong 'Still off' verdicts — the most expensive lie a verification tool can tell.
risks.mitigation: Explicit non-empty-but-projects-to-zero check on BOTH sides → VerifyError.HierarchyUnusable, abort before any verdict. Kept distinct from the empty-snapshot case, which still degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH exactly as AC-41 requires.

risks.text: The Skiko trap: if any diff code drifts into an ImageBitmap-typed helper, the feature's own tests stop compiling or throw LibraryLoadException.
risks.mitigation: Exactly one file (RegionPixels.kt, ~10 lines) mentions ImageBitmap, with a KDoc note saying why; RegionDiff/VerifyVerdict/BeforeAfterFormat take primitives only; no test constructs a bitmap.

risks.text: dumpHierarchy costs ~2.7 s and N region diffs follow, so a naive implementation reads as a frozen window and the user clicks Verify again.
risks.mitigation: VerifyPhase (Loading → Recapturing → Diffing → Ready) in reduced state drives a visible progress UI (NFR-15); all decode/diff under withContext(Dispatchers.Default); verifyJob cancellable from ExitVerify, a second Verify, MarkAllVerified or a device change (the dumpJob precedent).

risks.text: Reusing resolveAndSend() as 'unchanged' needs a pendingFollowUpBatchId hook; a sloppy edit could make every normal send try to write FollowUpSent.
risks.mitigation: Nullable field, null-checked, cleared in a finally; one ViewModel test asserting a plain (non-follow-up) send writes no status at all.

risks.text: The 0-based (history) vs 1-based (envelope) crop index resurfaces when renumbering the follow-up annotations.
risks.mitigation: Never read crop-N.png, so there is exactly one conversion point: the mapIndexed building StagedAnnotation(index = i + 1). One test over a 2-of-3 still-off selection asserting indices are 1 and 2, not 0 and 2.

risks.text: Verify requiring a live mirror session (AS-1 corrected) reads as a bug on the History tab ('I clicked Verify and got an error').
risks.mitigation: VerifyError.NoLiveSession renders a specific, actionable ErrorState naming the device to start mirroring, not a generic failure.

risks.text: Scope creep: F-9 touches data, database, domain, repository, presentation and the shell call site at once.
risks.mitigation: Steps are ordered so the read path (1-4) and the pure verify core (5-6) are independently testable and mergeable before any UI exists; the UI steps (7-11) cannot start the arithmetic over.

risks.text: An annotation that was already correct and that the agent correctly left alone reads 'Still off' under change-evidence semantics.
risks.mitigation: Taken knowingly as the cheap error — a false 'Still off' costs one click of 'Mark all as verified'; a false 'Fixed' destroys trust in the whole tool. Documented in VerifyVerdict's KDoc as the accepted ceiling.

risks.text: A deliberate `wm density` change between send and verify silently relabels the BEFORE side in the new density.
risks.mitigation: Unmeasurable in v1 (density was never persisted) and strictly better than labelling everything in raw px. Recorded as a data gap with the densityDpi-column migration as the written-down upgrade path.

functional.text: On any sent batch (not gated on a 'Fixed' status, since nothing in v1 is confirmed to set one), provide a 'Verify' action that re-captures the live screen and diffs it, per annotation box, against the original frozen frame; matches mark the annotation resolved, mismatches surface a one-click follow-up that re-stages that single annotation for re-send.
Remove the BatchStatusModel.Fixed gate on the History row's Verify button (MirrorHistoryTab.kt HistoryEntryRow trailing slot) so it renders and is clickable for every sent batch regardless of status.

On Verify click, enter a Verify phase that re-captures the live device frame and hierarchy for the device that sent the batch (AS-1/AS-2, AS-1 as amended below), reusing the existing mirror capture pipeline rather than a new one.

[AMENDED — correction #1, overrides clarify decision #4] For each annotation, read the matching region from the frozen and re-captured frames via ImageBitmap.readPixels(startX, startY, w, h) — a commonMain member, with the annotation rect as the region arguments — and compute the pixel-region diff as pure IntArray arithmetic in commonMain (no PixelDiffer seam, no expect/actual, no fun interface for the diff itself). A separate fun interface BatchFileReader (desktop java.io impl, null-returning Android/iOS stand-ins, matching the BatchFileStore/CropEncoder pattern) is added solely to read frame.png and crop files off disk.

For each annotation, re-run F-5 measure-mode's node matching against the re-captured hierarchy and compare it to the original stored measurement, producing a dp-delta result string in the same format as live measure-mode (e.g. 'top Δ6dp → 0dp').

[AMENDED — correction #2, change-evidence semantics] Mark an annotation's verdict 'Fixed' iff: the hierarchy node matched on both sides AND the matched node's layout finding is gone in the AFTER measurement AND the pixel region shows change-evidence (regionPx < MIN_REGION_PIXELS, where the ratio is statistically meaningless and the hierarchy half decides alone, OR changedRatio > REGION_CHANGE_RATIO). Anything else — including an unmatched hierarchy node — is 'Still off', never silently skipped as 'Fixed'.

Render the Verify view per design-verify-view.md as a new phase inside the existing MirrorHost/MirrorContent composition (no second MirrorHost call site): two 296×640 frames (BEFORE/AFTER) with per-annotation rects coloured by verdict, a 300px 'Verification' panel with result rows and verdict words, an 'AGENT CHANGES' section cut for v1 (see out-of-scope), footer actions 'Send follow-up · N' and 'Mark all as verified', a four-step header strip, and a '← Back to live' chip that resets to the live mirror with the History tab selected.

'Send follow-up · N' re-stages exactly the N still-off annotations (plural; AC-42) into a new AnnotationEnvelope sourced from the re-captured (AFTER) frame and its crops — not the stale frozen frame — renumbered 1..N for the envelope, and re-enters F-7's send path via MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend by reusing resolveAndSend() unchanged except for one pendingFollowUpBatchId hook that writes Follow-up sent on its success path.

'Mark all as verified' force-sets every annotation's verdict to Fixed without further diffing and writes the batch status to Verified; if a run is still in progress it cancels verifyJob first so a late completion cannot overwrite the override.

Persist verify outcomes through HistoryRepository.updateStatus: Verified when a run ends with every annotation Fixed (or via the Mark-all override), Follow-up sent immediately after a follow-up send succeeds (written on the ORIGINAL batch; the follow-up itself records its own new Sent row). No v1 code path writes In progress or BatchStatusModel.Fixed — that remains an intentional gap (see out-of-scope).

If the re-captured frame's pixel dimensions differ from the stored frozen frame's, abort the diff before any per-annotation comparison runs and surface an error state (SizeMismatch) rather than comparing misaligned regions.

Reconcile the crop-index convention mismatch (0-based in history storage, 1-based in the AnnotationHandoff envelope) by never reading crop-N.png on the read side at all — the diff loop reads full-res frame.png plus stored rects, which strictly dominates the crops and makes the conflict vanish there. The only conversion point is the follow-up envelope build (mapIndexed → StagedAnnotation(index = i + 1)), where history's 0-based iteration order is renumbered 1-based for F-7.

nonFunctional.text: History and batch metadata persist locally and survive app restarts.

All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes. Satisfied in-place by the already-shipped VerificationRow/VerificationOutcome molecule and Theme.color.sentFixed/warnStillOff tokens.

Re-capture and the per-annotation diff loop run off the UI thread (Dispatchers.Default, consistent with AnnotationHandoff's existing suspend contract) and show a visible in-progress state (VerifyPhase: Loading/Recapturing/Diffing/Ready), since N region diffs plus a ~2.7s hierarchy dump can take long enough to need one.

A device disconnect mid-verify aborts the run cleanly: no partial status write, the original batch status is untouched, and the user lands in a retryable state rather than a stuck spinner. Reuses the existing flatMapLatest(sessionDeviceId) teardown that already cancels in-flight jobs.

MET-3's <5% false-positive target is not automatically verifiable in this codebase in v1 — there is no golden before/after dataset and no Compose UI-test harness. Diff thresholds (CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR, REGION_CHANGE_RATIO, MIN_REGION_PIXELS) are named tunable constants with stated ceilings, validated by manual spot-check only; MET-3 is recorded as unverified-in-v1 rather than asserted by an automated test.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any sent batch, when the user clicks 'Verify', then the app re-captures the live screen and diffs it, per annotation box, against the stored frozen frame using a pixel-region diff plus a hierarchy/layout diff of the matched node.

[AMENDED — correction #2, change-evidence semantics replaces the self-defeating literal wording] Given a Verify diff, an annotation is marked 'Fixed' only when its hierarchy node matches, its layout finding is gone in the AFTER measurement, AND its pixel region shows change-evidence (regionPx < MIN_REGION_PIXELS, or changedRatio > REGION_CHANGE_RATIO); given any of these fails, the annotation is 'Still off' and a one-click follow-up re-stages exactly the still-off annotations for re-send. The original wording ('no material difference → resolved') is rejected because it would report an agent that changed nothing as having fixed the bug.

Given the History tab, when a row's batch status is anything other than Fixed (e.g. Sent), then the Verify button is still rendered and clickable — the BatchStatusModel.Fixed gate at MirrorHistoryTab.kt:179 is removed, superseding F-8's AC-36.

Given Verify is clicked, when the re-captured frame's pixel dimensions differ from the stored frozen frame's (resolution or orientation changed), then no per-annotation diff runs and an error state is shown instead of a misaligned comparison.

Given a Verify run, when an annotation's original hierarchy node cannot be matched in the re-captured hierarchy (moved, renamed, or removed), then that annotation's verdict is 'Still off' regardless of its pixel-region diff result.

Given at least one annotation is 'Still off' after Verify, when the user clicks 'Send follow-up · N', then exactly the N still-off annotations are re-staged from the re-captured (AFTER) frame and crops and sent through F-7's existing send path, and the batch status updates to Follow-up sent.
Given a Verify run completes with every annotation 'Fixed', or the user clicks 'Mark all as verified', then the batch status updates to Verified via HistoryRepository.updateStatus.

Given a Verify run is in progress (re-capture or diffing), when the device disconnects, then the run aborts, the original batch status is left unchanged, and the user can retry Verify once reconnected.
Given the diff reads image bytes for comparison, then it reads the full-resolution stored frame.png (never crop-N.png, never the ≤128px thumbnail BLOB), reusing stored rects for region extraction.

architecture.approach: A thin new read path down the existing layer stack, one new pure internal package in presentation-feature-mirror (core/verify/), one new stage case inside the existing MirrorHost composition, and one new plain StateFlow for the two bitmaps. The verify run is a single cancellable suspend function on verifyJob with seven ordered steps: (1) snapshot sessionDeviceId + currentHeld.value atomically — null held ⇒ NoLiveSession; (2) GetSentBatchUseCase(batchId) — null/failure ⇒ NotOnDisk; (3) decodeToImageBitmap the stored frameBytes and compare its IntSize to the live HeldFrame's — disagree ⇒ SizeMismatch, abort before any per-annotation work (from here there is exactly ONE IntSize and ONE density for both sides); (4) DumpHierarchyUseCase(deviceId) for the AFTER hierarchy, phase = Recapturing (the ~2.7 s cost); (5) projectMeasureNodes both snapshots against that one shared IntSize — non-empty-but-zero-candidates on either side ⇒ HierarchyUnusable and abort, while an empty-to-begin-with snapshot degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH (AC-41); (6) per annotation i (history's 0-based order): measure() both sides, regionPixels + changedRatio, verdictOf, beforeAfterLabel — then publish VerifyFrames and reduce the rows; (7) all rows Fixed ⇒ UpdateBatchStatusUseCase(batchId, Verified), otherwise write nothing. Device identity is re-checked at every suspension point; a change or null ⇒ Disconnected with no status write.
architecture.rationale: Every choice is the highest rung of the ladder that holds. Reuse an existing commonMain API (ImageBitmap.readPixels) over inventing a seam — a seam here would be an interface with one implementation AND would push the arithmetic into desktopMain where desktopTest has no Skiko, destroying the testability that is the whole point. Reuse an existing oracle (F-5's findingOf) over a new layout-diff algorithm. Reuse an existing model (SentBatchModel) over a new read-model type. Reuse an existing composition (MirrorStage) over a new Destination. Reuse an existing send path (resolveAndSend) over a new envelope pipeline. Reuse an existing molecule (VerificationRow, whose @Preview already uses the design's exact strings) over a new row. The only genuinely new seam is BatchFileReader, because BatchFileStore is write-only and there is no okio/kotlinx-io in the catalog — that gap is real and is not the pixel gap. Status writes happen last and only at terminal points, which makes NFR-16's 'no partial status write' true by ordering rather than by a transaction.

errorStates.behavior: VerifyPhase.Loading (reading the batch off disk) then Recapturing (the ~2.7 s dumpHierarchy) then Diffing (the per-annotation loop). Each phase renders its own label in the Verification panel; the frames appear as soon as VerifyFrames is published, rows fill in as the loop advances. Never a bare indeterminate spinner with no text.
A batch with zero annotations shows an empty Verification panel, 'Send follow-up · 0' hard-disabled, and 'Mark all as verified' as the only sensible action.
VerifyError.NoLiveSession — ErrorState naming the device and telling the user to start mirroring first, then retry (AS-1 as amended; this must read as a precondition, not a failure).

VerifyError.NotOnDisk — the row's framePath/hierarchyPath is null or the file is gone/unreadable (a stored path is a hint, never a guarantee). The Verify button is still rendered per AC-39; the honest failure happens here, not as a second status-shaped gate.
VerifyError.SizeMismatch — the live frame's IntSize differs from the decoded frame.png's (resolution or orientation changed). Checked ONCE, before any per-annotation work (FR-46/AC-40).

VerifyError.HierarchyUnusable — the AFTER dump failed, or a non-empty snapshot projects to ZERO candidates (the documented Pixel 8 984×2132-vs-1080×2400 display-override case). Abort before any verdict rather than emitting N confident wrong 'Still off' results. Distinct from an empty-to-begin-with snapshot, which degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH per AC-41.

VerifyError.Disconnected — sessionDeviceId changed or went null at any suspension point. No status write, the original batch status untouched, and the state is retryable once the device is back (NFR-16/AC-44).

A follow-up send that fails (handoff.publish failure) leaves the ORIGINAL batch status untouched — FollowUpSent is written only after resolveAndSend reaches its success point — and surfaces through F-7's existing SendPhase.Failed path with no new error surface.

logs: MirrorViewModel log.i on verify start: batchId, annotation count, live frame size (replaces the existing stub's single log.i line).
log.i per terminal outcome: Ready with n/N fixed, or the VerifyError case name — one line per run, not per annotation.
log.w when projectMeasureNodes returns empty for a non-empty snapshot, including both frame sizes — this is the display-override landmine and it must be diagnosable from a log alone.
log.i on each status write (batchId, status) so the two previously-unexercised BatchStatusModel values are traceable.
No per-pixel or per-annotation logging — N region diffs would flood the log for no benefit.
metrics: Wall-clock of the dumpHierarchy step and of the whole diff loop, logged once per run, so the ~2.7 s KDoc budget can be re-checked against real hardware without a profiler.

changedRatio per annotation is held in memory for the run (not persisted, not rendered — the design shows measurement deltas, never pixel percentages) and is the number a manual MET-3 spot-check reads out of the debugger.

accessibility.requirement: The verdict is never colour-only: VerificationRow pairs the accent colour with a ✓ / ! GlyphBadge AND the literal word 'Fixed' / 'Still off'. The AFTER frame's verdict-coloured rects keep their numeric badges, which tie each rect back to a labelled row.
Both verdict tokens (Theme.color.sentFixed, warnStillOff) are identical in light and dark and already shipped with contrast reviewed — no new colour token, so NFR-9 parity holds by construction.
'Send follow-up · N' keeps F-7's ⌘↩ hint and is reachable by keyboard; it is hard-disabled (not merely dimmed) at N = 0 so the keyboard path cannot fire a no-op send.
Every error state renders a title AND a description through ErrorState — no icon-only or colour-only failure. NoLiveSession in particular names the required action ('start mirroring this device').
The in-progress phase is announced in text ('Recapturing…', 'Diffing…'), not as a bare spinner, so the ~2.7 s wait is legible rather than ambiguous.
The '← Back to live' chip is a real focusable control with a text label, not a bare glyph; it is the single documented exit from the stage.
Result lines use Theme.typography.monoData at the design's size via tokens only — no hardcoded sub-10px text is introduced.

performanceBudget.target: ~2.7 s measured on a Pixel 8 — budgeted, not optimised. It must be the only adb round trip in the run (the AFTER frame costs one atomic currentHeld.value read) and it must be visibly staged as VerifyPhase.Recapturing.
~100 ms for a 300-node dump (F-5's documented KDoc budget), i.e. ~2N×100 ms for the loop; projectMeasureNodes runs ONCE per side, not per annotation.
O(w·h) single pass, integer-only, two IntArray allocations (one per side) and no per-pixel allocation. A 200×60 region is 12k pixels — immeasurable next to the dump.
The first phase change reduces within one frame of the Verify click; no step may leave the window without a text label for more than ~100 ms.
Every decode/project/measure/diff step inside withContext(Dispatchers.Default); nothing on the intent context; the UI thread only ever receives reduced value types and two already-decoded bitmaps.
Rows are reduced in one batch at the end of the loop (or at most once per annotation), never per pixel; VerifyFrames never enters reduced state at all.
At most two full-res bitmaps plus two per-region IntArrays alive at once; the stored frameBytes are released after decode and crop files are never read.

dataHandling: BatchFileReader reads absolute paths that came out of this app's own Room database and were written by FileSystemBatchFileStore under ~/.rectify/history/<sanitised batchId>/. Screenshots, hierarchy XML and comments never leave the machine. The follow-up envelope goes through F-7's existing local file-slot handoff; F-9 adds no network call and no new egress point.
Decoding stored bytes is wrapped and degrades to null (VerifyError.NotOnDisk) rather than crashing on a corrupt or truncated PNG — null-on-failure is universal in this repo.
No new persisted data: no new column, no new file on disk, no new preference. The only writes are two BatchStatusModel values through the existing updateStatus.
permissions: None new. The feature requires an already-authorised adb connection and an active mirror session, both established before Verify is reachable.
privacy: Frame pixels live in memory for the duration of the run and in the already-existing on-disk history directory. F-9 neither prunes nor extends that directory — the documented ponytail ceiling (nothing prunes ~/.rectify/history) is inherited from F-8 and explicitly not addressed here.

migrations: None. @Database stays at version 1 and no Migration is written — this is a deliberate, recorded decision (densityDpi comes from the fresh AFTER dump, because a migration could never retroactively supply density for rows already on disk). Adding the column later remains the written-down upgrade path and would then need a real version bump plus a hand-written Migration per database.md.
rollout.backwardCompatibility: Fully backward compatible with every batch F-8 already persisted: the read path uses only columns that already exist, and a row whose framePath/hierarchyPath is null (or whose files were deleted) surfaces VerifyError.NotOnDisk instead of failing. Existing statuses render unchanged — the status chip stays informational and no longer gates anything. F-7's normal send path is byte-for-byte unchanged apart from one null-checked hook, and a plain send still writes no status.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Kotlin/Native release linker OOMs (Java heap space) under ~4 parallel linkReleaseFramework tasks against a 4 GiB daemon heap. Pre-existing, affects every cross-target gate in this repo.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The mandatory ./gradlew :presentation-feature-mirror:build cross-target gate failing with Java heap space rather than a real compile error.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Tautological test (assertEquals(1, PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION)) that would pass under any edit — the test was the defect.

knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Do NOT write a test over the constants' values. Test the BEHAVIOUR they gate: changedRatio over hand-built IntArrays that straddle the floor, and verdictOf over the eight conjunct combinations. Thresholds are tunable by design (NFR-17), so pinning their literals would actively obstruct tuning.

knownRisksFromQA.description: A test whose name and comment claimed a structural property the body never asserted (the body asserted Empty → empty twice).
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: VerifyVerdictTest or VerifyStageDerivationTest claiming 'aborts before any verdict' or 'unmatched node is Still off' while actually asserting something weaker.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Each test name states exactly one claim and the body asserts that claim; the HierarchyUnusable test asserts the rows list is EMPTY (no verdict was produced), not merely that an error is set.

knownRisksFromQA.description: core/payload file names do not partition their contents — one label function in PayloadLabels.kt while two live in PayloadEstimate.kt, and PayloadGate.kt accumulated three unrelated predicates.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The new core/verify/ package drifting the same way — e.g. the verdict rule leaking into RegionDiff.kt, or thresholds inlined at call sites.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Five files, one concern each, fixed up front: RegionPixels (the ImageBitmap edge), RegionDiff (the metric), VerifyThresholds (the constants), VerifyVerdict (the AND-rule), BeforeAfterFormat (the formatter). The AND-rule exists in exactly one expression in exactly one file.

knownRisksFromQA.description: ROOT CAUSE: promptOverride carries no record of the payload it was authored against, so nothing can distinguish a stale override from a deliberate one.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The follow-up re-stage inheriting a stale promptOverride from the original (pre-verify) frozen frame and silently sending the agent the wrong prompt.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: The follow-up builds a FRESH FrozenFrame over the AFTER HeldFrame with promptOverride explicitly null (comments are re-sent verbatim — the closed decision), so no override can leak across the verify boundary. One test asserts the re-staged frame's promptOverride is null.

knownRisksFromQA.description: ClearStaged kept promptOverride, resurfacing a prompt for deleted annotations (fixed in F-7, same defect class as F-1).
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same lifecycle hole in the new ExitVerify handler — leaving VerifyUiState, verifyFrames or pendingFollowUpBatchId set after leaving the stage, so a later unrelated send writes FollowUpSent on an old batch.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: ExitVerify cancels verifyJob and clears all three (state, frames, pending id); pendingFollowUpBatchId is additionally cleared in a finally on the send path. One test asserts a plain (non-follow-up) send writes no status at all.

knownRisksFromQA.description: A crop cell fitted to a constant 84dp but drawn in weight(1f), clipping the outline at narrow panel widths — arithmetic done against an assumed size rather than a measured one.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same class of bug in the verify stage: the design fixes the frames at 296×640, but a real device frame has its own aspect ratio, and the panel is resizable.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Render each frame aspect-correct WITHIN a 296×640 box (letterbox, never stretch — stretching a frame in a pixel-verification tool misrepresents the thing being verified), and derive the annotation-rect overlay from the SAME measured frame box via FrameGeometry's render leg, never from the nominal constant.
